chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Yunus, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

A man performing Tamattu' who did not have a sacrificial animal with him, he said: 'He fasts three days: the day before Tarwiyah, the day of Tarwiyah, and the day of Arafah.' I said to him: 'When he enters the day of Tarwiyah, and it is not appropriate for him to fast in Mina during the days of Tashriq, he said: 'So when he returns to Mecca, he fasts.' I said: 'If his companions hurry him and refuse to stay in Mecca, he said: 'Then let him fast on the road.' I said: 'Does he fast while traveling?' He said: 'Yes, he fasts on the day of Arafah, and the people of Arafah are traveling.'

The reasoning for the obligation of these three days while traveling is that it is attached to the specific days, which are the days of Dhi al-Hijjah. Whenever the pilgrim enters the state of Ihram and has not yet fasted them, the obligation of these three days is lifted from him, and he is required to offer the blood (sacrifice) of a sheep.

key_terms.التَّرْوِيَةِ: The 8th of Dhi al-Hijjah, when pilgrims proceed to Mina
key_terms.التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of 11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhi al-Hijjah
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: The 12th month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.عَرَفَةَ: The 9th of Dhi al-Hijjah, the day of standing at Arafah
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعٍ: A pilgrer who performs Umrah first, then Hajj, keeping the Ihram intact
key_terms.هَدْيٌ: Sacrificial animal offered by the pilgrer

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a Mutamatti' pilgrer who does not have a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the substitution of fasting for the sacrificial animal (hady) in the Tamattu' Hajj when the pilgrim lacks the means or opportunity to sacrifice. It establishes that the three days of fasting are tied to specific dates in Dhu al-Hijjah, allowing them to be fulfilled even while traveling if necessary, thereby emphasizing the flexibility of ritual obligations in Hajj jurisprudence. The text further notes that if these days are missed before entering the state of Ihram, the obligation shifts entirely to the blood sacrifice (dam).
